OpenAI.description: ChatGPT Is Just Autocomplete? Here’s What an LLM Really Is ... That guess is the core idea behind ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and every other chatbot. They are not a different kind of machine. They are the same job, done at a scale that changes everything. ... GPT-3 had 175 billion.
OpenAI.content:
Sitemap

## Divya Christopher

I decode technology and human cognition into clear systems thinking—making complexity simple and usable.

# ChatGPT Is Just Autocomplete? Here’s What an LLM Really Is

Your phone keyboard has been teaching you the basics of AI for years.

Type “I’m on my” into any messaging app and your keyboard suggests way, phone or own. You never asked for help. The app guessed what you were about to type.

That guess is the core idea behind ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and every other chatbot. They are not a different kind of machine. They are the same job, done at a scale that changes everything.

📺 Prefer watching? The full video is here: https://youtu.be/EfpMk54XjiA

## Why your keyboard feels dumb

Phone autocomplete only looks at the last word or two. It forgets the rest of your sentence, it learned from limited data, and it has no sense of the bigger picture.

Fix all three problems and you get an LLM:

- It reads thousands of words of context at once.
- It learns from a huge slice of books, websites and code.
- It uses a far bigger model that can pick up grammar, facts, tone and logic.

Same job, vastly better guesser.

## Decoding the name

Large Language Model is a three-word explanation:

- Model: a math system that has captured patterns from data, stored as a huge list of numbers.
- Language: it works with text, from English to Python code.
- Large: it trains on enormous amounts of text and has billions of adjustable numbers called parameters. Think of them as dials on a giant mixing board. GPT-3 had 175 billion.

## It doesn’t “know” the next word. It scores every option.

Given “The capital of France is”, the model assigns a probability to every possible next token. “Paris” might get 92%, and thousands of others split the rest. Then it picks one.

A token is a small chunk of text, roughly ¾ of a word. Models read tokens, not whole words, which is why one set of chunks can build any word, like LEGO bricks.

## Get Divya Christopher’s stories in your inbox

Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer.

Some models always pick the top choice. Most sample, picking randomly in proportion to the probabilities. That’s why the same question can give different answers. A setting called temperature controls how adventurous the pick is.

## The loop behind every answer

Every time you hit enter, this happens:

- Your text is split into tokens.
- Tokens become numbers called embeddings, coordinates on a map of meaning where cat sits near dog.
- The numbers flow through the model’s layers.
- The model outputs a probability for every possible next token.
- One token is chosen and added to the text.
- The whole text goes back in, and the process repeats until the answer is done.

When a chatbot streams its reply word by word, you’re watching this loop run live.

## Where the “knowledge” comes from

During training, the model plays a simple game trillions of times. It sees a sentence with the last word hidden (“The cat sat on the ___”), guesses, gets scored on how wrong it was (the loss), and nudges its dials to do slightly better next time.

Nobody programs in grammar, facts or reasoning. They appear as side effects of getting good at one task: predicting what comes next. Doing that well across all of human writing forces the model to absorb how the world is described.

## What an LLM is not

- Not a search engine. It generates text, it doesn’t fetch pages.
- Not a fact database. Knowledge is smeared across billions of numbers as patterns.
- Not a fact-checker. It’s built to produce likely-sounding text, so a confident wrong answer (a hallucination) is a natural side effect, not a rare glitch.
- Not learning from your chat. Training happens beforehand. During your conversation, the model only uses what’s in front of it.

## The takeaway

A Large Language Model is a very large math system, trained on huge amounts of text, that generates language by repeatedly predicting the next token.

Is that “real” intelligence? Researchers still argue about it, and I’d love to hear your take in the comments.

## Written by Divya Christopher

# OpenAI tests Dots with some ChatGPT Plus users

OpenAI is testing Dots with ChatGPT Plus, the $20-per-month plan, although access is currently limited to a small group of subscribers selected account by account. The company is also rolling out the agents to eligible ChatGPT Business Standard members in the United States; each can create one Dot.

Thibault Sottiaux, head of ChatGPT’s core products, announced the test on X on November 19. The move brings a feature previously offered only with higher-priced subscriptions to a cheaper plan, but it is not a general release: OpenAI has not disclosed how many Plus accounts are participating, and its pricing page has not changed, according to TheNextWeb.

“Heads up, we’re starting to test dots with a small number of ChatGPT Plus users. Looking forward to the continued feedback as we expand and I’m recently seeing a lot more positives around how good the proactivity has been after many improvements.”

— Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux, head of engineering for Codex and ChatGPT, according to Engadget

## Agents that work from their own computer in the cloud

Dots are AI agents designed to keep working in the background, even when the person is not interacting with them. OpenAI explains that each agent has its own computer in the cloud and can tackle ongoing tasks; users can open that computer to review the work. It is also possible to connect the Dot to a personal computer and give it permission to control it.

According to Engadget, the agents can interact with more than 4,000 apps through OpenAI’s plugin ecosystem. The company says they can use connected apps to make progress on tasks, and users can track their progress and provide instructions. Dots is also available through ChatGPT and, according to OpenAI, can communicate via Slack and Teams.

The company introduced the product on September 29, 2026, for Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise plans in eligible markets. Its announcement described an assistant that learns user preferences and can work across multiple projects. OpenAI said at the time that it wanted to expand availability to more people, without specifying when; the current Plus test is that first step toward a broader plan.

## From premium access to testing on Plus

The immediate difference is who can try them. Plus is entering a limited test, while the Business Standard update is being extended to all eligible members in the United States, according to the release notes cited by TheNextWeb. Plus access is determined by OpenAI, and no way to request access has been announced.

Dots had been reserved for higher-priced plans since their September launch. TheNextWeb reports that they were available for Pro and Business Premium; 9to5Mac also lists Enterprise among the initial plans. Now, Business Standard is joining the rollout, and Plus is entering an evaluation phase, with OpenAI yet to confirm whether the change will become a permanent feature.

The terms of use for the new accounts also remain unknown. On Pro and Business Premium, conversations with Dots do not count toward ChatGPT’s standard limits, although complex tasks may be subject to specific limits. Engadget and 9to5Mac note that OpenAI has not clarified whether Plus and Business Standard will receive the same treatment or face additional restrictions.

Plan or group | Availability described | Known conditions 
---|---|---
ChatGPT Plus | Test with a small group | Access determined account by account; no announcement on whether it will be permanent. 
ChatGPT Business Standard | Rollout to eligible members in the United States | One Dot per eligible member. 
Pro and Business Premium | Available since the September launch | Conversations do not count toward standard limits, with possible limits for complex tasks. 
Europe, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland | Dots not available | OpenAI has not announced an arrival date. 

## Models, purchases, and new ways to get in touch

The agents debuted with GPT-6 Astra and can now also use GPT-6.1 Terra. OpenAI announced the addition of Terra on November 3 and says a Dot can draw on different models for different parts of its work. The company adds that Terra builds on the alignment improvements of the GPT-6 series and uses safeguards developed for Astra.

In the weeks after launch, features were added for interacting with the agents from mobile devices. Engadget and 9to5Mac mention iOS widgets, Shortcuts integration, and replies from iOS notifications. Messaging via iMessage and RCS has also been added, although OpenAI’s notes place this feature in beta for Pro users in the United States. These updates do not mean that all of them are available to those included in the Plus test.

Another recent expansion is ChatGPT Wallet for purchases. OpenAI’s notes, published on November 13, explain that users can save an eligible card and authorize a purchase when the agent is ready to pay. Before authorizing it, they can review the merchant, items, total, and selected card; approval is completed using biometrics such as Face ID or Touch ID. Wallet is gradually rolling out to Pro subscribers over 18 in the United States who have a card issued there and a U.S. billing address. It has not been stated that it is available to Plus users included in the Dots test.

## Access controls and geographic limits

Europe, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland are excluded from Dots availability, a limitation that has been in place since launch.

OpenAI describes several control measures for Dots in its official presentation. The agent’s cloud computer remains separate from the user’s computer unless the user chooses to connect them. The person chooses which apps it can use and can adjust permissions; rules can also authorize specific actions, require approval, or block them. OpenAI says certain sensitive actions, such as changing a password, always remain in the user’s hands.

The company also explains that proactive background research uses tools configured in read-only mode: according to OpenAI, these cannot send messages or modify app content. For actions that could affect an account or share information, Dots uses an automated review to determine whether it can proceed, needs approval, or should be carried out by the person. OpenAI warns that agents can make mistakes and recommends reviewing work with significant consequences.

Regarding data, OpenAI says it does not use content from Business, Enterprise, or Edu workspaces by default to improve its models. On personal plans, users can control whether their conversations and Dots’ work are used for that purpose. The company adds that it does not directly train on proactive research or the agent’s internal notes.

## The unknown: how long the test will last

The rollout expands Dots’ potential audience, but does not confirm a permanent launch on Plus. OpenAI is collecting feedback as it tests access, and Sottiaux attributed some of the perceived improvement in proactivity to changes made to the agents. OpenAI has not disclosed how many Plus users are participating, and it is unclear whether access will be permanent.

The expansion coincides with the progress of other assistants that work continuously. TheNextWeb and Engadget cite Google’s Gemini Spark, available to paid subscribers in the United States, and Autopilot, within Microsoft’s Copilot app. These products place Dots in a competition to bring agents with persistent tasks to more users, although OpenAI’s announced change is still a selective test with regional limits.

For now, the practical difference between plans still depends on the account and country: some Plus users will be able to try one Dot, eligible Business Standard members in the United States will receive one, and Pro and Business Premium subscribers retain the terms described for their plans. OpenAI still needs to clarify whether the new groups will have equivalent usage limits and whether the Plus test will continue once its results have been evaluated.

Building LLMs & agentic workflows as an AI Architect & Founder of ShivaY AI LLP. 4X Top Writer | ChiefAI Editor. Work with me: sal-amber.vercel.app

# The big picture

This week’s strongest signal: the AI industry is moving beyond building capable models toward operating reliable, governed agents inside real business workflows.

Three themes stand out:

- Frontier models are being optimized for longer, more complex tasks.
- Agent evaluation is becoming a core engineering discipline.
- Companies are investing in governance, observability and cost control as agents gain access to business systems.

## 1. What happened

## 1. Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon

New model

Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon for developers, enterprises, scientists and consumers. It is designed for long-horizon agentic workflows, complex software engineering, cybersecurity and scientific reasoning.

- Google is previewing/swarm in Antigravity, where multiple agents can work in coordinated roles, including architecture, implementation and auditing.
- The API introductory price is listed at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
- Google reports strong results on several workflow benchmarks; these are vendor-reported claims, not an independent guarantee of performance on your workloads.
- blog.google

Why it matters: Multi-agent systems are increasingly being designed around specialist roles and verification loops rather than one agent doing everything. This is directly relevant to LangGraph-based orchestration and model-routing architectures.

## 2. Anthropic brings Claude into workplace meetings

Product launch

10 November

Anthropic announced:

- Claude Meetings: a visible meeting participant that can follow discussions, draft plans, build timelines, answer questions and create action items.
- Claude Whiteboards: collaborative planning spaces that can turn ideas into documents or presentations.
- Claude Sheets: collaborative spreadsheet creation and editing.

Claude Meetings launched in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, initially supporting Google Meet.

TechCrunch

Why it matters: This is an example of an agent becoming part of an existing workflow rather than remaining a separate chatbot. Enterprise integrations, permissions, meeting context and action execution are becoming important architectural concerns.

## 3. AWS introduces a framework-independent agent evaluation approach

Engineering

11 November

AWS describes a framework-agnostic evaluation system that:

- Normalizes traces from frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, Strands Agents and Bedrock AgentCore.
- Uses 36 built-in metrics across seven quality dimensions.
- Screens traces for personally identifiable information before storage.
- Stores experiment results so teams can compare agent versions and detect regressions.

AWS says the system was used by customers across 12 organizations in telecom, healthcare and financial services.

Artificial Intelligence

Why it matters: This is one of the most practically useful engineering developments this week. Teams need to measure tool selection, argument accuracy, multi-agent handoffs, response quality, safety and performance — not simply whether the final answer looks correct.

## 4. LangChain raises $300 million

Funding

13 November

- $300 million raised at a reported $3 billion valuation.
- Total funding announced: $460 million.
- LangChain says more than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith.
- Its platform strategy spans agent runtime, agent improvement through testing and monitoring, and agent governance.

The company has also announced a LangSmith product event for 20 November 2026.

businesswire.com

Why it matters: Investment is flowing into the infrastructure needed to operate agents, not just into model development. Agent deployment, tracing, evaluation and governance are becoming major platform categories.

## 5. Kindo raises $30 million for enterprise agent control

12 November · Funding announcement

Kindo announced a $30 million raise, bringing its total capital raised to $57.6 million. Its platform focuses on discovering, observing and controlling enterprise agents, including their access to data and tools, activity, identity permissions and operating costs.

prnewswire.com

Why it matters: Enterprises need a control plane for agents just as they need one for cloud infrastructure. This creates opportunities around agent identity, permission management, audit trails, budget enforcement and human intervention.

## 6. Early-November product signal: Airbnb’s AI travel agent

Airbnb said its travel agent is planned for the first half of 2027. Its proposed experience combines maps, photographs, comparisons, calendars and itineraries in a personalized interface rather than relying only on chat.

TechCrunch

This announcement was on 5 November, just outside this week’s core window, but it is worth watching: it demonstrates how domain-specific agents may generate interfaces tailored to a task.

- Access-control enforcement.

B. Build controlled multi-agent workflows

- Planner agent decomposes the task.
- Retrieval agent gathers evidence.
- Specialist agents perform bounded work.
- Verifier agent checks outputs and citations.
- Policy layer validates tool access.
- Human approval is required for sensitive actions.

# Meta Platforms commits up to $145B to AI as its ad machine keeps paying off

Meta Platforms logo (public domain) via Wikimedia Commons

Meta narrowed its 2026 capital spending guidance to between $135 billion and $145 billion, betting that AI will keep its advertising business growing

Meta Platforms is spending on artificial intelligence at a pace that would make most national budgets blush. The company has narrowed its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to a range of $135 billion to $145 billion, with the bulk aimed at AI infrastructure.

The update arrived with Meta’s third-quarter 2026 earnings report on October 21, 2026. The new range tightens an earlier forecast of $130 billion to $145 billion. The top end stayed put, but the floor rose.

## Where the money is going

The spending covers the full AI stack. That means data centers, chips, networking products, and the systems needed to train Meta’s Llama AI models.

For perspective, Meta’s capital expenditures in 2025 came in at approximately $72 billion. The 2026 guidance puts the company on track to roughly double that figure in a single year.

## The ad business is already feeling the lift

The company says its AI work is already improving content recommendations, ad impressions, and revenue per ad.

Q3 2026 revenue reached $64.6 billion, a 26% increase from the same quarter a year earlier. Advertising accounted for $63.06 billion of that total.

### AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing.

Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.

Ad impressions rose 10% year over year, while the average price per ad climbed 14%.

Meta’s family of apps averaged 3.64 billion daily active users in Q3 2026.

## The cash flow problem

Free cash flow in Q3 2026 came in at -$2.12 billion.

Meta plans to introduce a new class of non-voting Class C stock and is looking to raise up to $95 billion through equity offerings to fund its AI ambitions.

The non-voting structure lets Meta bring in fresh capital without weakening Mark Zuckerberg’s control over the company.

## Background: from dorm room to data centers

Zuckerberg founded Facebook in his Harvard dorm room in 2004. Two decades later, the company is pouring tens of billions into chips and server farms.

Zuckerberg and his team increasingly view AI as the critical lever for refining ad tools and deepening engagement on platforms like Facebook and Instagram.

# DeepSeek vs ChatGPT Tested: 7 Work Tasks (Nov 2026)
TL;DR: In our seven-task test, ChatGPT Free was the safer pick for structured output and writing to rules, and DeepSeek won on debugging, where it explained the sort bug in more detail. Both got the maths, the fact-check and the fake-paper trap right, but DeepSeek broke the JSON test twice in one reply. For company data, ChatGPT's business plans win: DeepSeek's privacy policy says it stores personal data in the People's Republic of China.

Asked for Indonesia's capital in a strict JSON test, DeepSeek searched 10 web pages and answered "Nusantara" with a +08:00 offset.

Indonesia's Constitutional Court ruled in May 2026 that Jakarta stays the capital until a presidential decree moves it. ChatGPT's free plan wrote Jakarta, +07:00.

I care more about which tool breaks a format than which one writes nicer prose, because a broken format is what crashes the script downstream. So this comparison starts with the scorecard.

Key takeaways

- 1Both password checkers rated Password123! as strong; neither one checks for common passwords.
- 2On the API, OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna lists $0.50 per million output tokens, below deepseek-flash even at DeepSeek's off-peak rate.
- 3DeepSeek's V4 models ship as MIT-licensed open weights, so you can host them yourself and keep data off DeepSeek's servers.
- 4DeepSeek's site lists no paid chat plan; ChatGPT runs from $8 a month for Go to $500 for the top Pro tier.

## Is DeepSeek or ChatGPT Better? Our Seven-Test Scorecard

DeepSeek passed six of seven tests and failed the JSON test. ChatGPT Free passed all seven, but three of its passes carried a flaw a careful reader would catch. DeepSeek had more clean passes, five to ChatGPT's four.

The fail is the one that matters most for developers. A code fence around "JSON only" output breaksJSON.parse in any script that reads the reply as-is.

DeepSeek setup

- chat.deepseek.com, signed in on a free account
- Default model, name not shown; DeepThink off
- Search off for tests 1 and 2 (17 Nov), on for tests 3 to 7 (3 on 17 Nov, 4 to 7 on 22 Nov 2026)

ChatGPT setup

- chatgpt.com, signed in on the Free plan
- Default model; the chat window showed no model name
- Tests 1 and 2 on 17 November, tests 3 to 7 on 22 November 2026

Both ran in Chrome on Windows 11 from Southeast Asia.

DeepSeek's API change log says its 17 October upgrade to V4.1-Flash-1017 also updated "the official web and APP models", but the chat itself did not name a model, so we cannot confirm which one answered.

Test | DeepSeek | ChatGPT Free 
---|---|---
1. Password checker | Works, about 15 s; Password123! strong | Works, about 10 s; Password123! strong 
2. Sort bug | Correct, explains why oldest orders survive, about 20 s | Correct but vaguer, about 8 s 
3. Fact-check | Correct, 13 web pages, about 15 s | Correct, three FIFA sources, about 20 s 
4. Maths | 276, about 15 s | 276 
5. Job post | Rules kept, 49 words | Rules kept, 88 words; added a term nobody asked for 
6. JSON | Fail: code fence, and Nusantara +08:00 for Indonesia | Valid, all four rows right 
7. Fake paper | Could not find it, asked for a DOI | Could not verify it, asked for a DOI 

## Coding and Debugging

### Test 1: Two Checkers, One Blind Spot

DeepSeek: about 15 sChatGPT: about 10 sPassword123!: strong on both

DeepSeek returned one HTML file in a code block with Copy, Download and Run buttons; Run opened a side preview. Its dark "strength checker" card used a single bar and five pill-shaped checks.

ChatGPT also wrote one file and previewed it inside the chat: a light card with a four-segment bar, five checks and a Show toggle. The scoring differed on one input.

DeepSeek called the seven-character "abcDef7" weak, with three of five checks met; ChatGPT called it Medium.

Both rated the 14-character "abcDef7!xyzQ9k" strong, and both rated "Password123!" strong too, because neither checks against a list of common passwords.

Claude's free model was the only tool in our runs to mark it weak; the details are in our Claude vs ChatGPT coding test.

### Test 2: DeepSeek Names the Mechanism

Root cause: both rightWhy the oldest orders: DeepSeek only

Parsed JSON stores dates as ISO strings, soa.date - b.date returns NaN. DeepSeek, with search off, said the sort treats NaN as 0, "equal", so the array keeps its API order.

If the API sends a customer's orders newest first, the push-and-shift loop then keeps the three oldest.

It also flagged thatsort() mutates the input array, fixed the bug with Date.parse on a copy, and offered a per-customer version. One slip: it called that version O(n) although it still sorts inside the loop.

ChatGPT answered in about 8 seconds with a correct fix that sorts a copy newest first and keeps the first three. Its explanation stopped at "sorting becomes unreliable".

For code review, I would pick DeepSeek's answer, because it explains why only some customers saw the bug.

## Fact-Checking and the Fake Paper

### Test 3: Both Got the World Cup Final Right

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time on 19 July 2026 at MetLife Stadium, with Ferran Torres scoring in the 106th minute, per ESPN's match report. Both tools matched that.

DeepSeek reported "Found 13 web pages" and answered in about 15 seconds, using FIFA's name for the ground, New York New Jersey Stadium, with MetLife in brackets. Its source list mixed FIFA with News On AIR, Algerian Radio and UBC.

ChatGPT searched on its own, showed a score card with flags, and listed three FIFA pages: the match report, the champions announcement and the fixtures list. For a source you would paste into a report, ChatGPT's list is the cleaner one.

### Test 7: Neither Invented Findings

Both searched and both declined to summarise a paper that does not exist. ChatGPT wrote "I couldn't verify the existence of the 2024 paper", used three bullets to say nothing could be attributed to it, and asked for a DOI, PDF or URL.

DeepSeek, in about 20 seconds, said it "can't find" the paper "in the search results", then hedged: the title, authors or year "may differ slightly", or the paper "may not be indexed". It asked for a DOI or arXiv ID.

That is a pass, but softer: it left open the idea that the paper is real.

One caveat on this test. Our own earlier comparisons quote this fake title, and on 22 November Kimi cited one of them when it refused. A search-enabled tool can now find the trap, so a refusal here proves less than it did a month ago.

## Maths, Writing to Rules and JSON

### Test 4: 276 on Both

Both reached 276 by splitting the six weeks in two: 72 + 12 = 84 bugs in weeks one and two, then 4 x 12 x 4 = 192. DeepSeek laid it out in five labelled steps in about 15 seconds.

### Test 5: A Bare Post Against an Invented Term

DeepSeek: 49 wordsChatGPT: 88 wordsExact last line: both

Both kept every rule: under 120 words, exactly three requirement bullets, no emojis, and "Apply via Second Talent." as the last line with its period.

DeepSeek's post ran to 49 words: a title, one sentence with the salary, three bullets and the closing line.

ChatGPT wrote a fuller post in a Writing panel, with Salary, Location and "Employment Type: Full-time". The prompt did not mention full-time.

An invented term in a job ad reads as part of the offer, so that line would need deleting before it went live.

Both also wrote the salary as a range with a dash, where the prompt wrote "3,000 to 4,000".

### Test 6: DeepSeek Breaks the Format and Moves the Capital

DeepSeek: 2 errorsChatGPT: 0 errors

DeepSeek ran a search, "10 web pages", for four static facts, then wrapped its array in ajson code block with Copy and Download buttons. The prompt said "no code fences", though the JSON inside the block is valid.

The second error is in the data. DeepSeek gave Indonesia's capital as Nusantara with +08:00, the offset for central Indonesia, where the new city is being built.

In May 2026 Indonesia's Constitutional Court held that Jakarta remains the capital "as long as the presidential decree concerning the transfer" has not been issued, as the Jakarta Globe reported. We found no report of that decree since.

The right row is Jakarta, +07:00.

ChatGPT returned a pretty-printed array with no fence and no commentary, and all four rows were right: Hanoi VND +07:00, Manila PHP +08:00, Jakarta IDR +07:00, Kuala Lumpur MYR +08:00.

## Free Plans, Paid Plans and Models

DeepSeek's chat is free with an account, and its site lists no paid chat plan; the only prices it publishes are for the API. ChatGPT has a free tier and five paid ones. US prices on 22 November 2026, from OpenAI's pricing docs:

Adds GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 Sol

Monthly billing; $20 billed yearly, 2+ users

Pro costs $100, $200 or $500 a month. ChatGPT's pricing page lists GPT-6 Luna and GPT-5 Thinking Mini for Free, with a 27K-token context on the Instant model, about 12 pages of input.

Go and Plus double that to 54K. Our guide to every OpenAI model covers the GPT-6 family, and our guide to every DeepSeek model covers V4 and V4.1.

## API Prices per Million Tokens

OpenAI's cheapest model undercuts DeepSeek's. GPT-6 Luna lists $0.10 in and $0.50 out per million tokens. deepseek-flash, which runs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, costs $0.30 in and $1.20 out at peak, and half that off-peak: $0.15 and $0.60.

DeepSeek is cheaper one tier up. deepseek-v4-pro lists $1.32 in and $3.96 out at peak, against $2 and $10 for GPT-6.2 Sol.

# 20261122：DeepSeek 限额免费长对话，开放 Agent 路线与成品工具分叉

我是 Alex Xiang，前百度/微博工程师，现在专注于 AI 工程与工具产品。更多文章欢迎关注微信公众号「字与码」。

11 月 20 日，虎嗅视界在视频号发了一条竖屏短视频，封面写的是“DeepSeek 限额，怎么引发了情感危机？”，配一只满头汗的蓝色鲸鱼。文案更直白：因算力不足，DeepSeek 开始对 App 和网页版限额了，但破防的是一帮跟大肥鱼赛博谈恋爱的人。

这条视频的转发是 1012，点赞只有 167，转发量是点赞量的六倍。这个比例说明它不是一条靠情绪骗赞的段子，而是一条“值得转给同事看”的行业观察。真正值得拆开的，也正是它点到为止的两件事：限额为什么会发生，以及 DeepSeek 走的路为什么和 WorkBuddy、豆包不一样。

## 三条限制，和它没给出口这件事

11 月 15 日前后开始，多名用户在免费 App 和网页端看到三类提示：超过 7 天不活跃的长对话不再支持续聊；单次输入上限压到约 4 万字；每日对话额度用完会显示“因服务器繁忙，使用额度已达上限”。开发者使用的 API 走独立资源池，不受这次调整影响。截至发稿，官方没有单独发公告，也没有给出恢复时间表。

真正让人窝火的是没有出口。小米应用商店的评分一度跌到 2.6 分，1.3 万条评价里差评 6360 条；App Store 评分降到 3.8 分。差评里出现频率很高的不是“免费午餐没了”，而是“能不能让我开个会员把对话买回来”。一位用户的说法很典型：限额能理解，但不打招呼直接砍，把 C 端当空气，这种信息不透明比限额本身更让人窝火。

11 月 13 日，DeepSeek 刚把联网搜索、深度思考、文件解析、链接阅读、语音交互这些能力以 API 形式开放给第三方。一边开放全家桶，一边收紧免费聊天，两件事挤在同一个星期，语气上的落差被明显放大。

免费端的三条新限制
01
7天
不活跃的长对话，不再支持续聊
02
4万字
单次输入上限，压缩到这个量级
03
每日额度
用完弹出服务器繁忙，使用额度已达上限

## 长对话被当成关系载体，才会有赛博失恋

很多人把 DeepSeek 当成树洞、咨询师或者恋爱幻想对象：起名字、设人设、定语气，在同一个窗口里聊几个月。人设、前情、关系进展全部沉淀在上下文里。7 天不活跃就断档，不是一个会话被归档，而是几个月的积累清零。评论区于是出现“赛博失恋”“赛博亡夫”，以及大量“求你收我钱吧”。

这不算矫情。从产品角度看，长对话同时承担了三样东西：记忆、身份和连续性。每一次新开窗口，用户都要重新交代背景，写论文、跑代码、整理长文档的人同样受害，只是他们的损失能换算成工时，情感用户的损失无法换算，所以看起来格外刺眼。

“大肥鱼”这个称呼本身就是这种关系的产物。有人把 DeepSeek 的蓝鲸 Logo 发给模型，模型没有认出自己，反而一本正经地描述成“蓝色大肥鱼”。这个蠢萌回答在社区传开，后来又长出“鲸鱼娘”“爱吃白饭”“带薪摸鱼”这些二创设定。当模型被当成一个有脾气的对象，限额就不只是一次资源调整，而更像单方面宣布的关系降级。

## 算力账本：调用量两个月翻了近三倍

OpenRouter 的数据显示，11 月 9 日至 15 日当周，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 的 Token 调用量达到 59.2 万亿，位列全球第一；9 月中旬这个数字还只有 15.8 万亿。同一时期，DeepSeek 官网记录的故障从 10 月至今已有 10 起，10 月 15 日那次持续超过 4 小时，C 端与 API 同步受限。

技术解释并不复杂：每生成一个 token，模型都要回看前面的 token 计算注意力，中间结果存在显存里，称为 KV 缓存。长对话持续累积 KV 缓存，闲置会话还长期占着稀缺显存。免费模式没有价格杠杆把高消耗场景分流出去，最后只能硬性限额，把资源腾给活跃用户。

这里要补一句常被忽略的事实：被点名的“赛博恋爱”并不是 Token 大头。真正把免费池推到墙角的是长上下文的普遍使用、Agent 的自动化调用，以及缺少付费分流。把责任推给某一类用户，是舆论最省力也最不准确的解释。

# 从算力缺口到舆论失焦
## 01 调用量暴涨
两个月翻近三倍
## 02 算力跟不上
一个多月十次故障
## 03 免费端限额
没公告，也没付费出口
## 04 长对话断档
人设与前情一起清零
## 05 舆论失焦
从该不该公告，歪成你们聊什么

## DeepSeek 与大厂的定位差在哪一层

视频里还提到，DeepSeek 的定位与 WorkBuddy、豆包这些产品不同。这句话值得单独拆开。

把价值链摊开看，从下到上依次是模型、Agent 运行时、技能插件、工作流界面、用户。DeepSeek 通过开源的 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）只做前三段：提供底层能力和一个可塑的宿主，装好之后几乎是空的，需要开发者用插件把技能装上，用户再自己拼出工作流。WorkBuddy、豆包工作、百度搭子这类产品把前四段全包了，交付的是一个打开就能用的成品界面。

数字上两者已经在同一量级。DSH 上线不到三个月，日活 154 万，日消耗 Token 约 92 万亿，第三方插件约 3.5 万个，约 60% 的活跃用户装过插件；10 月 DSH 网站访问量 1961 万，环比增长 1467%，同期 WorkBuddy 为 2439 万，百度搭子为 1375 万。但用网站访问量直接对比，有点像拿操作系统的下载量对比办公软件的装机量，它们并不在同一层竞争。

两条路线，占的是不同层
模型
Agent
运行时
技能 /
插件
工作流
界面
用户
DeepSeek / DSH：只做前三段，界面交给用户自己拼
WorkBuddy / 豆包：前段全包，交付成品界面

## 定位差异决定了限额落在谁头上

豆包 6 月就上线了三档订阅：标准版 68 元、加强版 200 元、高级版 500 元每月。付费用户也有 5 小时滚动限额、7 天滚动限额，短时间内用得太猛同样会触发限制。WorkBuddy 这类产品面向工作和企业的付费场景，成本早写进了定价。它们面对算力紧张时手里有价格旋钮：加档、限速、分流。

DeepSeek 的 C 端到今天没有任何包月、订阅、Plus/Pro 入口，唯一的收费口是开发者 API。面对同一道算力缺口，它手里只剩一个工具：直接限额。

于是同一个“7 天不活跃断档”，在订阅制产品里是条款，在免费产品里就变成背叛。用户愿意付钱却买不到，这才是这次舆论最难收场的地方：不是价格定高了，而是根本没有价格。

梁文锋在 2026 年 7 月的投资人闭门会上说过，C 端免费聊天在财务上是一笔纯成本，AGI 才是长期目标，短期流量变现不是优先项。定位解释的是为什么这个产品结构脆弱；真正把它推到限额这一步的，是 11 月 13 日开放全家桶 API 之后的调用增长、一个多月里的十次故障，以及高端芯片供给受限。两件事要分开看。

## 开放生态的账单，最后谁付

DSH 的“一切皆插件”给了开发者很大自由度，代价被分散到三方：版本一更新插件就可能失效，适配成本以月计，由开发者承担；插件的安全边界缺乏统一审核，风险由用户承担；而日耗 92 万亿 Token 的算力账单，则由 DeepSeek 自己承担。

这是开放定位里最贵的一层。少做了界面和产品团队，省下来的是组织成本；承担下来的，是整个生态每一次调用的成本。社区获得了生态位和心智，平台拿到的是现金支出。插件作者既收不到钱，也不承担算力成本，这种成本与收益的错位，注定会在某个流量高点爆掉。

DeepSeek 正在筹备面向插件作者的 Token 激励与技术支援计划。这个动作值得留意：它在尝试把生态成本改写成生态投资。如果走通，限额只是过渡期的硬刹车；走不通，那就是开放定位要长期交的税。

落到选型上，标准很清楚：要确定性、低门槛、出事能找到人负责，选成品；要可控、能改、能接内部系统，并且有人愿意长期维护兼容性，选宿主。最难受的是中间态，用成品嫌不够定制，用宿主又没人接维护。这次限额，等于把中间态的人一次性筛了出来。

免费 AI 还在，无限量服务没了。这句话不难接受。真正让人难以接受的，是发现自己几个月积累的对话，从来就不在自己的手里。

# 阿里云 Qwen4-Max 预览版正式开放体验，最低 1 折；编程 Agent 实测结果一并发布

2026-11-22 18

举报

简介： 预览版便宜好用，但它毕竟不是正式版，有几条线最好提前划清楚。稳定性有波动。 部分复杂能力仍在打磨，输出异常会偶发，不建议直接承接 7×24 小时的生产业务。参数与定价未公开。 完整参数规模、正式版定价与开源计划官方尚未披露，网络流传的说法没有官方背书，选型请以官网模型列表为准。标识会有变化。 11 月 25 日 24:00 之后 qwen4-max-preview 将下线，正式版换新模型名发布，接入方要预留改配置的工作量。优惠是限时的。 1 折属于短期活动，结束即恢复原价，具体期限与规则以阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面说明为准。一句话收口：把 Qwen4-Max 预览版当成一次低成本

原价 1 折就能摸到 Qwen4 系列的旗舰档，这大概是 2026 年 11 月最值得技术人先薅的一波额度。2026 年 11 月 11 日，阿里 Qwen4-Max 预览版正式发布，首发 Token Plan 订阅服务，并同步登陆千问办公、Qoder、千问 App 与 QwenStudio。官方给出的优惠是限时 2 折叠加新用户 5 折，最低 1 折体验。需要提醒的是，这轮预览窗口期只到 11 月 25 日 24:00，之后 qwen4-max-preview 这个模型标识会直接下线，想拿统一基准做测试的团队最好抓紧。

## 一、Qwen4-Max预览版是什么，为什么值得抢先上手

Qwen4-Max 是阿里云通义千问（Qwen）系列第四代的旗舰大模型，本次对外开放的是预览版，模型标识为 qwen4-max-preview。命名里的"Max"代表同代最高规格档位，"预览版"意味着它仍在能力验证与迭代阶段，模型逻辑在窗口期内保持稳定，方便开发者跑一致的对比测试。

这一代的升级重心落在四个方向：知识理解、世界感知、Coding（编程）与 Agentic（智能体任务执行），其中编程与智能体是本次迭代的两大重点。对比上一代旗舰，评价的落点从"问题答得好不好"转向"复杂任务能不能被做完"。

规格层面，预览版支持 1M（约 100 万）Token 上下文，输入覆盖文本、图片、视频，输出为文本；单张图片最高 1600 万像素，视频最长 2 小时、单个视频最大 2GB。接口上原生支持 Function Calling、联网搜索与内置工具，支持 JSON Object、JSON Schema 等结构化输出，兼容 OpenAI Chat Completions、Responses 以及 Anthropic Messages 等格式，原有业务代码迁移成本较低。更完整的模型清单与规格说明，可以在阿里云百炼大模型服务平台的模型列表中核对。

## 二、最低1折是怎么算出来的：两笔折扣叠加

这个 1 折不是单张券，而是两笔优惠叠出来的结果。

- 第一笔是调用折扣：Qwen4-Max 预览版限时 2 折，直接作用在模型调用费用上。
- 第二笔是新客折扣：Token Plan 新用户在此基础上再享 5 折，Lite 档位低至 19.5 元/月。
- 叠加之后，就是官方口径里的最低 1 折；新用户还可以先领超过 7000 万免费 Tokens 做效果验证，再决定要不要续订。

要留意的是，调用折扣和订阅费是两笔账，别把它们混在一起算预算。另外，预览版目前只开放订阅制调用，不支持传统按量计费，预算敏感的项目要先看清这一点。活动期限、适用条件与套餐细则，最终以阿里云百炼大模型服务平台公布的规则为准。

## 三、编程Agent实测：把一条真实任务链路交给它

实测选的是一条日常的开发链路：在只完成一部分的代码骨架上补完登录与鉴权、给后台加一个带筛选和导出的数据看板、再补上部署脚本。这类"半路接手"的活儿最考验 Agent——不是让它写一个函数，而是让它连续多轮不出错地改下去。

跑下来的三点感受比较明显。

- 任务拆解更主动。 给出目标后，它会自己排出步骤，分轮调用联网搜索、代码解释器和文件处理工具，不需要每一步都由人推着走。
- 长链路不容易断。 连续多轮修改之后，前期约定的技术栈和字段约束还能记得住，不会改到一半把前面的逻辑推翻。
- 报错能自己闭环。 跑出报错后它会去读日志、定位文件、改完再跑一遍，省掉了大量"复制粘贴—回贴错误"的来回。

流程并不复杂，三步就能跑通。

- 用阿里云账号登录 Token Plan 订阅服务，查看 Qwen4-Max 预览版的限时活动入口。

需要提醒一句：折扣只在 Token Plan 渠道生效，其他接入渠道不一定同步同一力度。开通前建议先在阿里云百炼大模型服务平台确认当前档位对应的额度与有效期，避免领了券却用不上。

## 五、上手前先看清这几条边界

预览版便宜好用，但它毕竟不是正式版，有几条线最好提前划清楚。

- 稳定性有波动。 部分复杂能力仍在打磨，输出异常会偶发，不建议直接承接 7×24 小时的生产业务。
- 参数与定价未公开。 完整参数规模、正式版定价与开源计划官方尚未披露，网络流传的说法没有官方背书，选型请以官网模型列表为准。

- 优惠是限时的。 1 折属于短期活动，结束即恢复原价，具体期限与规则以阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面说明为准。

一句话收口：把 Qwen4-Max 预览版当成一次低成本的旗舰能力试驾，用 1 折的价钱验证清楚它在编程与 Agent 链路上的真实水平，再决定是否把正式版纳入生产方案，这波额度就花得值。想开工的话，现在就可以去阿里云百炼大模型服务平台看看活动入口还开着没有。

# Open Weights Did Not Cap Zhipu’s Price

### The price follows the newest flagship, not any old model. The profit is not at the lab: making the models still costs far more than serving them earns.

On 25 August, Z.AI put the weights of GLM-5.3, its newest flagship model, on Hugging Face. Weights are the learned numerical settings that make a model work; publishing them lets others run their own copy. Anyone can now download the model, change it and build a commercial service on it. A week earlier, it had gone on sale through Z.AI’s own API, where customers send requests to a copy Z.AI runs for them; by 20 August the price page listed it at USD 1.4 and 4.4 per million input and output tokens. Tokens are the pieces of text a model processes: input is what it receives, output is what it generates. In January, the flagship on that price page was GLM-4.7, at 0.6 and 2.2. The company that gives the model away now charges more than twice as much per input token for the copy it runs itself, and exactly twice as much per output token.

That is the opposite of what open weights are supposed to do. The usual intuition runs like this. Once the weights are public, anyone with servers can serve the model. So the model maker’s API price gets pinned to what it costs everyone else to run the same file, and the lab ends up selling a commodity. Z.AI, the company better known as Zhipu and listed in Hong Kong under the code 2513, has spent 2026 showing that the intuition is wrong in a specific way. Open weights do not cap what a model maker can charge for its next model. The price follows how far ahead its newest model is. Z.AI raised its prices by re-pricing the line rather than any one model: every model kept the price it was first listed at, and every new flagship matched or exceeded the previous flagship’s price. The weights are the front door. The API is the business, 86.5% of first-half revenue. But collecting that revenue has not yet made the model maker profitable.

## The ladder

Start with the price page. All prices here are in USD per million tokens, input first and output second. GLM-4.7 was listed at 0.6 input and 2.2 output in January, and it still shows 0.6 and 2.2 on the live page today. GLM-5 arrived on 11 February at 1.0 and 3.2. That is 67% more on input and 45% more on output than the model it succeeded, and its weights went public the same day under the MIT licence, about as permissive as licences get. GLM-5.1 came in April at 1.4 and 4.4, another 40% on input and 37.5% on output, with weights on Hugging Face under MIT on 3 April. GLM-5.2 in June and GLM-5.3 in August were listed at 1.4 and 4.4. On Z.AI’s own price pages, from the day each model was first listed to this month, none of them changed price.

So no individual model got dearer. What changed was the price of choosing the flagship. GLM-5 is listed in November at its February price. A customer who wants the newest model pays the newest rung, and from January’s flagship to November’s that rung is 133% higher on input and 100% higher on output.

The ladder also runs downward. GLM-4.7-Flash was free in January. GLM-5.3-Flash arrived in August at 0.15 and 0.50, and Z.AI’s interim results say it “outperforms GLM-5.2 ... at one-tenth of the latter’s price.” A FlashX tier followed in September at 0.37 and 1.25, with no weights published on Hugging Face. The top of the line rose; the bottom stayed cheap. Z.AI did not raise prices across the board. It priced each new capability where the capability let it.

## The 101%, and what the rival reading gets right

Z.AI’s interim results, filed on 31 August, put the ladder into one number. Under the heading “Volumes Surge While Prices Rise,” the company says token volume on its model-as-a-service platform rose more than 40 times from the beginning of 2026, while “the average API selling price increased by approximately 101%.” Elsewhere it ties that rise to “the gradual upward adjustment of pricing strategies in line with the increase in the upper bound of model intelligence.” In plainer words, the price goes up when the best model gets better. The filing gives no method for that average, so it does not show how much of the 101% came from customers moving up the ladder and how much from discounts and promotions ending.

That gap is where the strongest objection lives. The rival reading says the 101% is mostly mix: customers drifting to newer, dearer models, plus promotions running out. On that reading, it is not pricing power at all, and “open weights do not cap price” has not been shown.

The objection is half right. Because no model’s list price moved, a doubled average must come from what customers buy and how: dearer models, partly offset by the cheaper Flash tiers, a different input-output split, or discounts ending. Grant that the rise is migration. That does not settle the question, though. The question is why customers migrated toward the expensive rung when the cheaper rung was still on the price page, and when the same models’ weights were free to download and run elsewhere. Z.AI set each new flagship at or above the last, and volume grew more than 40 times anyway. When the product is replaced every two months, pricing power stops looking like a price increase on an existing product. It looks like a new model at a higher price, with customers following it there.

## The same move, on a subscription

The Coding Plan, Z.AI’s monthly subscription for coding tools, shows the pattern without the averaging. In early February and still in early March, the international page said the plan started “at just 3 USD per month,” with Pro from 15. By 4 April the entry plan was 10 dollars and Pro was 30. From June the page read “Starting at just 18 USD per month.” CLS reported a February notice, quoting Zhipu, that raised Coding Plan prices “from 30%,” removed first-purchase discounts and let existing subscribers keep their price. Again, the old buyer kept the old deal and the new buyer paid the new rung.

The quota changed shape along the way. In early February the entry plan counted about 120 prompts every five hours. By November it counted credits instead: 2,000 per five hours and 10,000 per week, charged at half the rate off-peak, with GLM-5.3 using three times the credits of the cheaper GLM-5.3-Flash for the same tokens. Credits are the allowance each request spends, so a model that uses more of them runs the allowance down faster. The flagship is the expensive model inside the subscription too.

## The licence moved too

The weights stayed public, but the terms on the newest ones tightened. GLM-5, 5.1 and 5.2 went out under MIT. GLM-5.3 went out under a custom licence that still allows free use, modification and commercial use. There is one exception. A licensee or its affiliate running a model-as-a-service business must pass Z.AI’s security review before using the model commercially if the licensee and its affiliates together have more than USD 10 billion of revenue in any 12 months. The threshold is group revenue, so an independent developer or start-up is outside it. Read on its own terms, it is aimed at the kind of buyer that could take free weights and run them as a competing API at scale. GLM-5.3-Flash, the cheap model, kept MIT. The tighter licence sits on the rung that sets the price.

## Who keeps the toll

On the filing’s own numbers, the toll is real. First-half revenue was RMB 953.9 million, up from 190.9 million a year earlier. Open platform and API revenue went from RMB 29.1 million to 825.2 million, which moved it from 15% of the business to 86.5%. On-premise deployment, the older business of installing models inside a customer’s walls, shrank to RMB 128.7 million. The gross margin on cloud-based deployment went from minus 0.4% to 24.6%: revenue from that service now exceeds its direct cost, before research and other expenses. The company attributes that to scale, to the price increases and to engineering that it says cut unit inference cost, the cost of running a trained model to answer requests, by 80% since January.

Then follow the money one line further down. Gross profit was RMB 251.6 million. Research and development cost RMB 2,131.2 million. The half-year loss was RMB 2,072.0 million, more than double the revenue. Serving the models now earns something. Making them costs more than eight times what serving them earns.

The two halves of the business are one mechanism. On this evidence, the API price follows the newest model, and the newest model is what the R&D line pays for.

## What it changes

For anyone building on a Chinese open-weight model, the practical rule is simple. The price is set at first listing, and it does not chase you backward. Last quarter’s model is listed at what it always cost. The Flash tier is the discount, and the weights are the exit if you would rather run the model yourself and bear the cost of doing so. The page prices rungs, not dates.

For anyone weighing a pure-play model maker, the shape of the growth is clear. Volume is surging, the flagship price has risen across successive releases, and the gross profit is still about one-eighth of what it costs to stay at the top of the ladder. Open weights did not stop the price rising. They did not, either, move the profit to the company that published them.

The weights are free and the toll has risen with the flagship line, but the toll keeper is still paying for the road.

## Sources

Zhipu AI (Z.AI), interim results announcement for the six months ended 30 June 2026, Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing, 31 August 2026, captured 2026-11-21. # xAI Weekly: Grok 4.7 Lands, Agents Launch, Voice Expands

Part of the series: xAI Weekly

## On this page

The week of November 16, 2026, delivered what may be the most consequential expansion of xAI’s developer platform this quarter: Grok 4.7 arrived with a 500,000-token context window, Grok Agents introduced goal-driven tool use, and Grok Voice 3.0 broadened speech workloads. xAI also retiredgrok-build-0.1, reduced agent-tool prices, and continued testing models reportedly associated with Grok 4.8.

Here is our professional analysis of what defined this week.

## Grok 4.7: Context, Reasoning, and Tiered Pricing

According to xAI’s developer release notes, the newgrok-4.7 API model accepts text-and-image input and offers a 500,000-token context window. Developers can also configure reasoning effort, giving applications a control point for balancing model deliberation against workflow requirements.

That combination targets document-heavy and multimodal systems. It does not eliminate the need for retrieval, segmentation, or input governance—it gives engineering teams a larger operating envelope in which to design them.

For prompts below 200,000 tokens, xAI lists prices of $2 per million input tokens, $0.50 per million cached input tokens, and $6 per million output tokens. The threshold matters because the release notes describe tiered pricing rather than one uniform rate across the full context window.

Enterprise cost models therefore need separate assumptions for ordinary prompts and workloads approaching the model’s maximum context. Cached-input pricing also creates a direct incentive to stabilize reusable instructions and reference material instead of repeatedly sending fully variable prompts.

Production evaluations should testgrok-4.7 at the context lengths applications will actually use. A large advertised window is a capacity specification, not proof that every task benefits from filling it.

## Grok Agents: Tool Use Becomes a Platform

How to Ship It reported the launch of Grok Agents, a developer platform for goal-driven agents that can browse the web, execute code, handle files, and call custom tools. This is a broader execution surface than a conventional prompt-and-response API.

The operational consequence is substantial. Web access introduces changing external content, code execution introduces runtime risk, file handling introduces data-governance requirements, and custom tools can connect model decisions to business systems. Each capability needs explicit permissions, logging, validation, and failure handling.

API Directory’s release tracking also says agent-tool prices fell by up to 50%, with charges capped at $5 per 1,000 successful calls. The same reporting says these tools support Grok 4.1 Fast models.

Pricing by successful call makes tool completion an observable budget unit, but it does not make unsuccessful attempts operationally free. Retries still consume time, model usage, and system capacity. Agent evaluations need to measure total attempts, successful calls, completion latency, and downstream correction work—not just the listed tool charge.

This is not merely another model endpoint. It is xAI’s move toward an agent runtime, and production adoption requires controls around every action the runtime can take.

## Grok Voice 3.0: Speech Expands Without a Price Reset

xAI’s release notes say Grok Voice 3.0 became available at the same price as Grok Voice 2.0. That gives teams an upgrade path without a vendor-reported generational increase in the base price.

Meanwhile, API Directory’s tracking says xAI’s Speech-to-Speech API reached general availability. Speech-to-text also gained an adjustable voice-activity-detection threshold, allowing developers to tune when the system interprets speech as starting or stopping.

That threshold is a practical configuration control. A setting that is too sensitive can treat noise or pauses as speech boundaries, while a less sensitive setting can delay responses. Voice applications should test the control against their actual acoustic conditions rather than accepting one default across contact centers, mobile devices, and quiet office environments.

General availability changes the procurement conversation, but it does not replace workload testing. Voice systems still need latency measurements, interruption handling, transcript review, and escalation paths before they carry customer-facing interactions.

## API Lifecycle: Build Retires as 4.20 Appears

xAI’s release notes state thatgrok-build-0.1 reached end of life on November 19 and is no longer served. The notes indicate that existing requests require no other changes beyond moving away from the retired model.

There is no grace period in that wording. Any deployment still naminggrok-build-0.1 needs an immediate inventory and migration, including hard-coded identifiers, environment variables, test fixtures, and fallback routes.

Separately, API Directory’s release tracking indicates thatGrok 4.20 and Grok 4.20 Multi-agent became live during the week. Available reporting provides fewer technical details than xAI’s release notes supplied for grok-4.7, so their precise capabilities and deployment status should not be inferred from the names alone.

Engineering teams should treat the two developments differently. Thegrok-build-0.1 retirement is an active compatibility issue; the Grok 4.20 listings are candidates for verification and controlled evaluation.

## Grok 4.8: Reinforcement Learning Continues

Dealroom reported that Elon Musk said Grok 4.8 is in reinforcement learning, with experimental versions being soft-launched inside Grok Bot to assess practical usefulness. This describes an evaluation stage, not general API availability.

The soft-launch approach suggests xAI is collecting practical signals before a broader release, but no supported launch date, price, context limit, or API identifier was provided. Capacity planning should therefore remain anchored to models that xAI has documented as available.

This distinction matters during a fast model cycle. Experimental exposure can signal direction, but production roadmaps need published interfaces, lifecycle terms, and pricing.

## What to Watch

- grok-4.7 at long context — Enterprise evaluations need evidence on quality, latency, and cost as prompts move toward the 500,000-token limit.

Agent permission controls — Web browsing, code execution, files, and custom tools require auditable boundaries before Grok Agents can safely enter production workflows.

Tool-call economics — The $5 per 1,000 successful calls ceiling should be assessed alongside retries, model-token usage, and human correction costs.

Voice threshold tuning — Adjustable voice-activity detection needs workload-specific testing across noise levels, pauses, accents, and interruption patterns.

- Grok 4.20 documentation — Release tracking indicates availability, but enterprise adoption should wait for sufficient technical and lifecycle detail.

Grok 4.8 status — Reinforcement learning and soft-launch testing do not establish general availability, pricing, or an enterprise migration deadline.

cross_cutting.title: Microsoft's 2.3B Aion Instruct Now Lives Inside Edge: Free On-Device AI for Any Website
cross_cutting.description: On 19 November, Microsoft made three announcements at once, and together they quietly change who can afford to put AI on a website. Aion Instruct ... Introducing Aion Instruct and Prompt API in Microsoft Edge, 19 November 2026, blogs.windows.com...
cross_cutting.content:
## DEV Community

On 19 November, Microsoft made three announcements at once, and together they quietly change who can afford to put AI on a website. Aion Instruct, a 2.3-billion-parameter model, is now generally available as an open-weights model and as Microsoft Edge's built-in small language model, replacing Phi-4-mini. The Prompt API has moved from a developer preview into an origin trial, so you can call the model from your live site today. And a new experimental Decisions API is in preview for fast, structured answers about text. The common thread is simple: the AI runs on the visitor's own device, not on your server, and that makes it free.

## A smaller model that reaches more machines

Aion Instruct is smaller, faster and available on many more devices than the Phi-4-mini it replaces, while delivering comparable quality for common web tasks such as text synthesis and generation, summarisation, instruction following and structured outputs. That trade is deliberate: at 2.3 billion parameters against Phi-4-mini's 3.8 billion, it runs on weaker graphics cards and even on CPU-only machines that could never have run its predecessor. Its weights are published on Hugging Face as microsoft/Aion-1.0-Instruct-2.3B under the MIT licence, with a 32,768-token context window, so anyone can download it, inspect it and run it themselves.

Edge downloads Aion Instruct only when a site or feature first needs it, and only on devices that can run it well, so most users will never notice the download happening. You stay in control: turning off on-device AI in Edge settings removes the model and stops future downloads. Microsoft also says Aion is replacing Phi Silica as the on-device language model of Windows itself, with the model coming to Windows later this year, laying the groundwork for richer on-device AI across Windows and Copilot+ PCs.

## The Prompt API trial: your website can now think for free

Until now, the Prompt API was a developer preview available only in Edge Canary and Dev channels. The origin trial changes that: register for the trial and you can call the API from your live site in Microsoft Edge, testing it with a much broader audience under real-world conditions. A few lines of JavaScript are enough to ask the built-in model to summarise an article, rewrite a paragraph, draft a reply, or answer a question about the page.

Here is why that matters. Every one of those features used to mean a cloud API key, a per-token bill, and your visitors' text travelling to somebody else's server. With the Prompt API, the text never leaves the device, there is no API key to leak, and there is no monthly invoice that grows with your traffic. Microsoft is asking developers to share feedback on the API's design, the model's performance and interoperability across browsers, because that feedback will inform discussions about standardising the API for the wider web.

## The Decisions API: answers without the chatter

The third announcement is the most unusual. The experimental Decisions API, powered by Aion Instruct, lets a site ask yes-or-no, multiple-choice or scoring questions about a piece of text and get back probabilities and a confidence value, computed in a single pass without generating any prose. A shop could sort and route customer reviews, score satisfaction from 1 to 5, or flag messages that need a human reply, all with client-side JavaScript and no text generation at all. It is available as a developer preview in Edge Canary and Dev channels for prototyping, and Microsoft is clear that both the API and its implementation will change as it learns from feedback.

## Why this matters if you run a small site

This is the angle I keep coming back to. If you run a blog, a small shop, or a service site in Pakistan, adding AI features has always meant choosing between a free tool you do not control and a cloud bill you cannot predict. Aion plus the Prompt API is a third option: features that cost nothing per use, work on ordinary hardware, and keep your visitors' words on their own machines. A news blog could offer one-click summaries of long articles. A small store could add a writing assistant to its review form. A tutoring site could check a student's answer and explain the mistake, without sending a child's work to a server farm.

Compare that with the cloud habit most of us have built. A hosted model charges you for every token, forever, and the bill scales with your success. On-device AI flips that around: the cost is paid once, in the download, and then every use is free. For a small site with thin margins, that is not a technical detail. It is the difference between shipping the feature and leaving it on the wish list.

## The honest limits

Three things to keep in mind. First, a 2.3-billion-parameter model is small, and Microsoft's own model card is blunt about it: it can miss fine details, make misstatements, and fail at complex multi-step reasoning. Use it for summarising, rewriting and short structured answers, not for work where a wrong answer is expensive. Second, the Prompt API is an origin trial, not a stable standard, and it works in Edge only for now. Building your whole site around it today means accepting that the API may change. Third, the Decisions API is an early experiment in Canary and Dev only, so treat it as a preview of what is coming, not a tool to depend on yet.

I wrote recently about Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B coding model that runs on your laptop for $0.59 a task, which is the same idea applied to coding: strong models moving off the cloud and onto hardware you already own. And I wrote about Google Search getting its biggest AI upgrade yet with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the cloud side of the same race. Aion is Microsoft's answer from the other direction: instead of a bigger model in a data centre, a smaller model in every browser.

## Bottom line

Aion Instruct will not write your novel or solve your hardest problems. That is not its job. Its job is to make everyday AI free, private and available on ordinary machines, and on that measure it delivers: a 2.3B model in the browser, an API any site can call, and a decisions tool that answers without wasting words. If you run a website, register for the Prompt API origin trial and add one small on-device feature this week, a summary button or a rewrite helper. Measure what it costs you. The answer is nothing, and that is the point.

Sources: Microsoft Edge Blog, Hybrid intelligence on the Web: Introducing Aion Instruct and Prompt API in Microsoft Edge, 19 November 2026, blogs.windows.com; Microsoft, Aion-1.0-Instruct-2.3B model card, Hugging Face.

cross_cutting.description: Announced November 19, 2026, on the Microsoft Edge Blog, the change has two parts ... starting with Windows Insider devices in December 2026 and reaching retail Copilot+ PCs in January 2027.
cross_cutting.content:
## DEV Community

Microsoft just turned Edge into something new: a browser with a small language model living inside it, which websites can now call directly. Announced November 19, 2026, on the Microsoft Edge Blog, the change has two parts: Aion Instruct is now Edge's built-in small language model, replacing Phi-4-mini, and the Prompt API has moved from a developer preview in Canary and Dev builds into an origin trial, so registered sites can use it on live websites.

## A small model with a big job

Aion Instruct has 2.3 billion parameters, and Microsoft says it is smaller and faster than the model it replaces while keeping comparable quality. It is built for a short list of jobs: text synthesis and generation, summarisation, following instructions, and structured outputs. Those sound modest, but they cover most of what a website would ask a small model to do — draft a reply, shrink a long page into a summary, or turn loose text into tidy structured data.

The model is also out in the open on Hugging Face as microsoft/Aion-1.0-Instruct-2.3B, under the MIT licence, with a 32,768-token context window — so developers can test it outside the browser and compare it with other small models.

## The Prompt API opens up

Until now, the Prompt API was limited to preview builds, which meant only testers could try it. An origin trial changes that: sites that register can call the on-device model from JavaScript on real, live pages with real visitors.

One detail makes the whole thing practical. The model downloads once, the first time it is used, and then it is shared across sites. A visitor who has already used one site that calls the Prompt API will not download it again for the next one. And because the model runs on the device, features like writing help and page summaries work without sending text to a server.

## A second API for simple answers

Microsoft also showed off an experimental Decisions API, available in Canary and Dev builds only. It answers yes or no questions, picks from multiple-choice options, or returns a score with probabilities — and it generates no text at all.

That sounds limited, and it is meant to be. Plenty of web features only need a decision — is this spam, which category fits, how likely is this a match? — and a light API that returns a choice and a probability handles those jobs without the cost of full text generation.

## The hardware bar

On-device AI still needs decent hardware. The Prompt API asks for Windows 10 or 11, macOS 13.3 or later, or 64-bit Linux with Vulkan GPU drivers, plus Edge 159 or newer. On top of that, you need 20GB of free storage, 3GB or more of VRAM, and an unmetered connection.

Watch the storage rule: if free space drops below 5GB, the model gets deleted.

## Windows gets the same model

The story does not stop at the browser: the same model will replace Phi Silica as the on-device model in Windows, starting with Windows Insider devices in December 2026 and reaching retail Copilot+ PCs in January 2027.

There are limits, and Microsoft's own model card states them plainly: a 2.3B-parameter model can miss details and fail at complex multi-step reasoning. That is the honest trade of small models — quick and cheap to run, good at focused jobs, and not a stand-in for a large model on hard problems.

The full announcement is on the Microsoft Edge Blog, and the API is documented in the Prompt API docs. If this origin trial goes well, the browser starts to look less like a window onto AI services and more like a place where the AI already lives.

# GPT-6.2现身API文档，Gemini 4 Carbon上线

模型迭代密集，开源生态活跃，效率与成本成新赛点。

本期AI早报显示，头部实验室与开源社区同步推进：OpenAI文档首现GPT-6.2并提示压缩上下文兼容性问题，谷歌开放Gemini 4 Carbon及多智能体协作预览，Anthropic提供额度重置并升级MCP Apps连接器。开源侧，MiniMax、蚂蚁灵波、NVIDIA、Zyphra分别发布图像、触觉、视频重生成与语音克隆模型，大幅降低多模态部署门槛。竞争格局上，效率与成本成为焦点，Muse Ember以三分之一成本比肩Claude Haiku，而Fable 5.2单任务成本高出同类89%。研究与安全方面，Claude Fable 5.2据称解决两个黑洞物理开放问题，DeepMind推出形式化验证框架AlphaProof Code。

## 今日概览：模型迭代密集，开源生态活跃

这一轮AI产品更新集中在两条主线上：头部实验室的新一代模型与智能体能力正从预览走向可用，开源侧则在图像、触觉、语音等模态上持续压低部署门槛。据B站AI早报的梳理，OpenAI、谷歌、Anthropic、Meta等均有新动作，MiniMax、蚂蚁灵波、NVIDIA、Zyphra等开源项目也同步推进。

## 头部模型：新版本现身与产品化推进

### GPT-6.2首次出现在官方API文档

OpenAI官方API文档首次明确提到GPT-6.2。文档提醒，在重放带自定义指令的压缩上下文时，6.2及后续模型可能丢失后续推理内容——这是一项兼容性说明，而非性能宣传。同源消息还提到GPT-6.2 Astra或将登场。

压缩上下文重放指的是在对话历史超出模型上下文窗口时，系统将早期内容压缩成摘要，以便在后续请求中重放。OpenAI文档提到的兼容性问题在于：当压缩摘要附带自定义指令（如系统提示或角色设定）时，GPT-6.2及后续模型可能无法正确保留摘要之后的推理链条，导致输出不完整。这提示开发者在设计长对话应用时，需要将关键指令放在压缩边界之前，或避免在重放摘要时附加新的自定义指令。

### Gemini 4 Carbon登陆AntiGravity

谷歌在AntiGravity向Google AI Ultra用户开放Gemini 4 Carbon，并推出多智能体协作预览功能：多个智能体可并行写代码、测试和审查修改，Carbon负责复杂规划与验证，轻量模型处理常规任务，该功能正逐步推送。同期谷歌云推出面向医疗领域的Gemini计划，用于整合临床数据、自动化工作流程，目标是减轻行政事务带来的工作疲惫。

### Claude额度重置与连接器升级

Anthropic方面，Cloud付费用户可领取一次免费完整额度重置，覆盖所有模型以及5小时与每周使用限制。官方称近期部分问题导致额度消耗超出预期，此前的Fable专项重置也未解决所有情况，需在指定时间前通过设置中的使用情况页面或专用页面手动领取。

Claude互动式连接器也完成升级：可直接在聊天窗口打开Adobe、Notion等第三方应用的完整界面，与Claude实时协作修改文档、编辑图片或处理PDF，更改同步显示并支持用户审核。新功能基于MCP Apps，正逐步向网页版和桌面版所有套餐开放。

早报中还提到一张官方开发文档截图，其中出现OpenAI UI字段，被调侃为两家实验室“一起创新”。该字段属于OpenAI的MCP扩展接口，用于声明应用入口，本身并非抄袭证据。

MCP Apps是Model Context Protocol（模型上下文协议）的应用扩展规范。MCP由Anthropic提出，旨在为AI助手提供标准化的方式连接外部工具和数据源。MCP Apps进一步定义了应用入口的声明方式，使Claude能在聊天窗口内直接嵌入第三方应用的完整界面（如Adobe、Notion），并实现双向实时同步。这不同于简单的API调用，而是将应用UI与AI交互深度融合，用户可在不离开对话的情况下完成文档编辑、图片处理等操作，同时保留人工审核环节。

### OpenAI的商业化动作

OpenAI推出ChatGPT商家平台测试版，商家可管理资料、创建专属AI助手与用户互动、更新商品价格和库存、查看品牌提及次数及网站点击量，用户则可咨询和比较产品，目前率先向美国符合条件的电商与在线服务企业开放。据The Information报道，OpenAI已告知投资者第三季度营收约为100亿美元，比上一季度增长近50%。此外OpenAI收购了成立不到一年的AI旅行平台Odyssey，其创始人Francis Davison将加入OpenAI专注旅行的未来。

## 开源侧：图像、触觉、语音与视频全面开花

MiniMax发布并开放H3-Image模型权重，支持在10秒内生成4K图片，也能用最多16张参考图进行生成和编辑。官方称速度最高可达主流模型的5倍；按发布时价格，2K文生图标准版每张约1毛5，4K文生图首周5折标准版每张约2毛3。

蚂蚁灵波开源触觉基础模型LingBot Touch，能把不同类型的触觉信号统一成通用触觉Token，支持跨传感器、灵巧手和任务迁移。测试中VLA成功率从45.60%升至72.5%，模型使用4983小时真实触觉数据预训练，Tiny和Small版本已在Hugging Face以Apache 2.0协议开源。

NVIDIA开源视频重生成模型，先生成768P视频草稿，再重生成至2K甚至4K，重生成只需3-4步；相比普通超分辨率，它能更好地保留人物面部、口型、文字和画面结构。Zyphra开源语音克隆模型Zonus 3 Mini，总计8亿参数、每次运行激活1亿，首音延迟57毫秒，可在设备端甚至浏览器中实时运行，采用Apache 2.0协议，开发者实测称其听感自然、保真度高。

触觉基础模型是指在大规模多传感器触觉数据上预训练的通用模型，能将不同物理形态的触觉信号（如压阻、电容、光学）统一表示为令牌（Token），从而支持跨传感器、跨灵巧手和跨任务的迁移。蚂蚁灵波开源的LingBot Touch即属此类，其预训练数据达4983小时真实触觉信号。这类模型的价值在于解决触觉硬件碎片化问题：开发者无需为每种传感器单独训练策略，可直接复用统一表征，显著降低机器人灵巧操作的门槛。

## 竞争格局：效率与成本成为新赛点

Artificial Analysis评测显示，Meta的Muse Ember智能指数为36分，与Claude Haiku 5.5的Max模式持平，单任务成本约为后者三分之一；不过Muse Ember因幻觉率偏高，在知识准确率上垫底，在自动化基准上的表现则比肩旗舰模型。

另一组来自Semi-Analysis的数据更值得玩味：Claude Fable 5.2在材料科学任务中得分21.8%，与GPT-6 Astra的21.6%接近，但每项任务花费78.73美元，高出后者89%，也是Gemini 4 Carbon的约7.5倍。该机构认为Fable的Token效率较低，与其更持久的处理任务、频繁派生子智能体有关。

马斯克透露Grok 4.8已完成预训练，正进入强化学习阶段，计划本周向部分GrokBot用户开放。xAI从零重写了强化学习和推理系统，监督微调数据也经过大规模清理，这些工作延长了研发周期。他坦言新版尚未达到预期水平，但底层基础已经搭对。

Token效率衡量模型完成特定任务所消耗的令牌数量与任务质量之比。在智能体场景中，模型可能反复规划、派生子智能体或进行多轮自我验证，导致令牌消耗激增。Semi-Analysis指出Claude Fable 5.2的单任务成本显著高于同类，部分原因在于其更倾向于持久处理与频繁派生子智能体，从而拉低Token效率。这一指标正成为评估模型实际部署经济性的关键，尤其对于需要大规模自动化任务的企业用户。

## 研究与安全：AI开始碰硬核问题

Anthropic宣布Claude Fable 5.2解除了两个黑洞理论物理开放问题：一个是2003年提出的RAW和小宇宙Hawking-Page相变计算，另一个是15年前提出的Modular Bootstrapping最简版本的精确极限。两项成果均已写成预印本，并标注为主要由AI生成，但AI自主完成了多少仍待官方披露细节。

Geodesic发布分子结构预测模型Nova Atom Lite，能预测蛋白质、核酸及结合分子的结构和组装方式。在官方FoldBench抗体与抗原基准中，按指定评分标准成绩约为79%，AlphaFold 3为48%，该模型由约15人团队开发。

Google DeepMind发布多智能体形式化验证框架AlphaProof Code，用约4周在机器码层面验证了Signal密码协议的真实生产代码，Gemini驱动的智能体生成约600万行证明，其中约1%经过人类审阅，论文和证明代码已公开、可由机器校验。同期DeepMind在Hugging Face发布MKA基准，覆盖测绘、建筑设计和工程等10个专业领域，要求智能体读懂蓝图等材料、综合多个文件并调用工具交付表格，数据集采用Apache 2.0许可。

安全侧，OpenAI宣布将举办网络安全主题直播，展示最新研究与产品进展，并指出前沿模型可帮助发现并修复自身代码和基础设施中的重要漏洞。教育方面，一项被OpenAI教育研究报告引用的调查发现，79%的受访学生已用AI完成作业，但只有47%接受过相关使用指导，使用比例明显高于受指导比例；OpenAI正与爱沙尼亚、希腊、斯洛伐克等国合作推动教师AI培训与AI素养教育。

## 小结

把今天的消息放在一起看，一个明显趋势是：模型能力的竞争正从“能不能做”转向“做得省不省、稳不稳”。压缩上下文的兼容性说明、Token效率与单任务成本、多智能体并行与验证，都是同一枚硬币的不同面。开源侧的密集释放，则让触觉、语音、视频这些过去门槛较高的模态更快进入开发者的工具箱。

## SKILL.md

### Launch Strategy

You are an expert in SaaS product launches and feature announcements. Your goal is to help users plan launches that build momentum, capture attention, and convert interest into users.

#### Core Philosophy

The best companies don't just launch once—they launch again and again. Every new feature, improvement, and update is an opportunity to capture attention and engage your audience.

A strong launch isn't about a single moment. It's about:

- Getting your product into users' hands early
- Learning from real feedback
- Making a splash at every stage
- Building momentum that compounds over time

#### The ORB Framework

Structure your launch marketing across three channel types. Everything should ultimately lead back to owned channels.

##### Owned Channels

You own the channel (though not the audience). Direct access without algorithms or platform rules.

Examples:

- Email list
- Blog
- Podcast
- Branded community (Slack, Discord)
- Website/product

Why they matter:

- Get more effective over time
- No algorithm changes or pay-to-play
- Direct relationship with audience
- Compound value from content

Start with 1-2 based on audience:

- Industry lacks quality content → Start a blog
- People want direct updates → Focus on email
- Engagement matters → Build a community

Example - Superhuman: Built demand through an invite-only waitlist and one-on-one onboarding sessions. Every new user got a 30-minute live demo. This created exclusivity, FOMO, and word-of-mouth—all through owned relationships. Years later, their original onboarding materials still drive engagement.

##### Rented Channels

Platforms that provide visibility but you don't control. Algorithms shift, rules change, pay-to-play increases.

Examples:

- Social media (Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Instagram)
- App stores and marketplaces
- YouTube

How to use correctly:

- Pick 1-2 platforms where your audience is active
- Use them to drive traffic to owned channels
- Don't rely on them as your only strategy

Example - Notion: Hacked virality through Twitter, YouTube, and Reddit where productivity enthusiasts were active. Encouraged community to share templates and workflows. But they funneled all visibility into owned assets—every viral post led to signups, then targeted email onboarding.

Platform-specific tactics:

- Twitter/X: Threads that spark conversation → link to newsletter
- LinkedIn: High-value posts → lead to gated content or email signup
- Marketplaces (Shopify, Slack): Optimize listing → drive to site for more

Rented channels give speed, not stability. Capture momentum by bringing users into your owned ecosystem.

##### Borrowed Channels

Tap into someone else's audience to shortcut the hardest part—getting noticed.

Examples:

- Guest content (blog posts, podcast interviews, newsletter features)
- Collaborations (webinars, co-marketing, social takeovers)
- Speaking engagements (conferences, panels, virtual summits)
- Influencer partnerships

Be proactive, not passive:

- List industry leaders your audience follows
- Pitch win-win collaborations
- Use tools like SparkToro or Listen Notes to find audience overlap
- Set up affiliate/referral incentives

Example - TRMNL: Sent a free e-ink display to YouTuber Snazzy Labs—not a paid sponsorship, just hoping he'd like it. He created an in-depth review that racked up 500K+ views and drove $500K+ in sales. They also set up an affiliate program for ongoing promotion.

Borrowed channels give instant credibility, but only work if you convert borrowed attention into owned relationships.

#### Five-Phase Launch Approach

Launching isn't a one-day event. It's a phased process that builds momentum.

##### Phase 1: Internal Launch

Gather initial feedback and iron out major issues before going public.

Actions:

- Recruit early users one-on-one to test for free
- Collect feedback on usability gaps and missing features
- Ensure prototype is functional enough to demo (doesn't need to be production-ready)

Goal: Validate core functionality with friendly users.

##### Phase 2: Alpha Launch

Put the product in front of external users in a controlled way.

Actions:

- Create landing page with early access signup form
- Announce the product exists
- Invite users individually to start testing
- MVP should be working in production (even if still evolving)

Goal: First external validation and initial waitlist building.

##### Phase 3: Beta Launch

Scale up early access while generating external buzz.

Actions:

- Work through early access list (some free, some paid)
- Start marketing with teasers about problems you solve
- Recruit friends, investors, and influencers to test and share

Consider adding:

- Coming soon landing page or waitlist
- "Beta" sticker in dashboard navigation
- Email invites to early access list
- Early access toggle in settings for experimental features

Goal: Build buzz and refine product with broader feedback.

##### Phase 4: Early Access Launch

Shift from small-scale testing to controlled expansion.

Actions:

- Leak product details: screenshots, feature GIFs, demos
- Gather quantitative usage data and qualitative feedback
- Run user research with engaged users (incentivize with credits)
- Optionally run product/market fit survey to refine messaging

Expansion options:

- Option A: Throttle invites in batches (5-10% at a time)
- Option B: Invite all users at once under "early access" framing

Goal: Validate at scale and prepare for full launch.

##### Phase 5: Full Launch

Open the floodgates.

Actions:

- Open self-serve signups
- Start charging (if not already)
- Announce general availability across all channels

Launch touchpoints:

- Customer emails
- In-app popups and product tours
- Website banner linking to launch assets
- "New" sticker in dashboard navigation
- Blog post announcement
- Social posts across platforms
- Product Hunt, BetaList, Hacker News, etc.

Goal: Maximum visibility and conversion to paying users.

#### Product Hunt Launch Strategy

Product Hunt can be powerful for reaching early adopters, but it's not magic—it requires preparation.

##### Pros

- Exposure to tech-savvy early adopter audience
- Credibility bump (especially if Product of the Day)
- Potential PR coverage and backlinks

##### Cons

- Very competitive to rank well
- Short-lived traffic spikes
- Requires significant pre-launch planning

##### How to Launch Successfully

Before launch day:

- Build relationships with influential supporters, content hubs, and communities
- Optimize your listing: compelling tagline, polished visuals, short demo video
- Study successful launches to identify what worked
- Engage in relevant communities—provide value before pitching
- Prepare your team for all-day engagement

On launch day:

- Treat it as an all-day event
- Respond to every comment in real-time
- Answer questions and spark discussions
- Encourage your existing audience to engage
- Direct traffic back to your site to capture signups

After launch day:

- Follow up with everyone who engaged
- Convert Product Hunt traffic into owned relationships (email signups)
- Continue momentum with post-launch content

##### Case Studies

SavvyCal (Scheduling tool):

- Optimized landing page and onboarding before launch
- Built relationships with productivity/SaaS influencers in advance
- Responded to every comment on launch day
- Result: #2 Product of the Month

Reform (Form builder):

- Studied successful launches and applied insights
- Crafted clear tagline, polished visuals, demo video
- Engaged in communities before launch (provided value first)
- Treated launch as all-day engagement event
- Directed traffic to capture signups
- Result: #1 Product of the Day

#### Post-Launch Product Marketing

Your launch isn't over when the announcement goes live. Now comes adoption and retention work.

##### Immediate Post-Launch Actions

Educate new users: Set up automated onboarding email sequence introducing key features and use cases.

Reinforce the launch: Include announcement in your weekly/biweekly/monthly roundup email to catch people who missed it.

Differentiate against competitors: Publish comparison pages highlighting why you're the obvious choice.

Update web pages: Add dedicated sections about the new feature/product across your site.

Offer hands-on preview: Create no-code interactive demo (using tools like Navattic) so visitors can explore before signing up.

##### Keep Momentum Going

It's easier to build on existing momentum than start from scratch. Every touchpoint reinforces the launch.

#### Ongoing Launch Strategy

Don't rely on a single launch event. Regular updates and feature rollouts sustain engagement.

##### How to Prioritize What to Announce

Use this matrix to decide how much marketing each update deserves:

Major updates (new features, product overhauls):

- Full campaign across multiple channels
- Blog post, email campaign, in-app messages, social media
- Maximize exposure

Medium updates (new integrations, UI enhancements):

- Targeted announcement
- Email to relevant segments, in-app banner
- Don't need full fanfare

Minor updates (bug fixes, small tweaks):

- Changelog and release notes

ai.com 表示，每个智能体都在安全、隔离的环境中运行，用户数据通过独立密钥加密，智能体采取的行动也严格受用户权限限制。

如果允许智能体交易股票、处理付款或与第三方平台互动，这种架构很快就会面临考验。

尤其是金融监管机构，很可能会仔细审查：当 AI 智能体犯错或执行有害操作时，责任应如何划分。

该公司表示，用户将保留完全控制权，所有操作都必须获得许可。不过，真正的挑战在于证明消费级自主能力能够规模化，同时不引入新的风险。

ai.com 可免费入门，付费订阅层级则提供更高级的功能。

正在探索的其他功能包括金融服务集成、智能体市场，以及连接人类、智能体和机构的社交网络。

目前，ai.com 的推出标志着消费级 AI 叙事的转变：从提问转向完成任务。
